question: The body of which of the following phyla is triploblastic, segmented and bilaterally symmetrical?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropoda**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthropoda**

 
 
• ​**The body of Arthropoda is triploblastic, segmented and bilaterally symmetrical.**
 
• **Invertebrate creatures** known as arthropods have a **segmented body, an exoskeleton, and paired jointed legs.** 
 
• Arthropods have an **external skeleton and are bilaterally symmetrical**. They must go through many stages of moulting, a process through which they lose their exoskeleton to reveal a new one, in order to continue growing.
 
• More than one million species of known **invertebrate animals** make up the four subphyla of Arthropoda: **Uniramia (which includes five classes of insects), Chelicerata (which includes three classes of arachnids and horseshoe crabs), Crustacea (which includes crustaceans), and Trilobita (trilobites).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Before arthropods, all animals only inhabited the ocean.** 
 
• They have **exoskeletons**, which means that they are covered in skeletons.
 
• They must **moult** (or lose) their skeleton in order to grow a new one as they get bigger.
 
• The most prevalent and well-known arthropods are **crayfish, scorpions, shrimp, lobster, insects, mites, and ticks.**
 
• Some species are so tiny that they depend on other arthropods to survive.
